facts.text: Riverside was first platted in 1868 and joined Jacksonville in 1887, marking the start of its transformation from plantation land to a thriving neighborhood.
The Cummer Museum of Art and Gardens, founded in 1961, houses one of only three major Meissen porcelain collections worldwide and sits on two acres of Italian and English gardens.
After the Great Fire of 1901, many displaced residents moved to Riverside, where wealthy citizens built riverfront mansions while others settled in modest bungalows further inland.
Riverside and Avondale together earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Districts, reflecting their rich architectural diversity and strong historic preservation efforts.
The neighborhood’s boundaries are roughly defined by Interstate 10 to the north and the St. Johns River to the east, framing a unique blend of urban and natural landscapes.
Named after Cincinnati’s Avondale neighborhood, Riverside’s early development was driven by the original Avondale plan created in 1920, a key moment in its growth.
